scope: Research-only continuation; six drafts, no READY, canonical species or schedules changed.
evidence_method: Reused accepted-name records. University, botanical garden, government and NPSOT morphology references paraphrased with citations; photographs not inspected or installed. Regional comparisons needing more evidence remain explicit.

species.look_here_first: Separate the central spadix from the surrounding pleated spathe. This is a cluster of tiny flowers, not one enormous flower. Also document the separate, tree-like leaf stage.
morphology_keys: Large flowering structure consists of a spadix surrounded by a spathe.
Actual flowers occupy the lower part of the spadix.
A large divided leaf is borne on a stalk during the leaf stage.
photo_roles: Spathe and spadix junction; lower flower zones only if already visible without damage.
Whole leaf and its branching pattern.
species.lookalike_work: Compare with other cultivated Amorphophallus; size or smell alone cannot establish species. Require exact accession/observation identity.

species.look_here_first: Find the narrow spathe and the long, slender spadix extending beyond it. Then examine the complete divided leaf above it, not a single leaflet.
morphology_keys: Usually one large compound leaf with multiple leaflets.
Slender spadix extends well beyond the narrow spathe.
Fruits form a cluster that becomes red.
photo_roles: Whole leaf with all leaflets visible.
Inflorescence profile showing spadix extension and its position relative to the leaf.
Fruit cluster attached to the plant.
species.lookalike_work: NC State distinguishes Pinellia pedatisecta by its disproportionately large central leaflet and inflorescence above the leaves. Final regional Arisaema-complex key and photo identity remain pending.

species.look_here_first: Look for the four conspicuous wings of the mature fruiting unit. Confirm the shrubby habit and small, grayish, scaly leaves; foliage alone is insufficient.
morphology_keys: Woody shrub with alternate simple leaves.
Leaves have a grayish surface with small scales.
Mature fruiting units show four prominent wings.
photo_roles: Fruiting branch showing leaves and attachment.
End and side views of a mature four-winged fruiting unit.
Leaf surface close-up and whole shrub.
species.lookalike_work: Compare mature fruiting structures with other Atriplex. The NPS account illustrates var. occidentalis; do not assign that variety to the unqualified species source record.

species.look_here_first: Examine the deeply divided leaf blade, then confirm with the flowers and flat seed pod on the same shrub or small tree.
morphology_keys: Shrub or small tree, often with multiple trunks.
Showy flowers are followed by flat legume pods.
photo_roles: Leaf face and attachment showing the cleft.
Flower front and side with a scale.
Attached mature pod and whole-plant habit.
species.lookalike_work: Other cultivated Bauhinia also have cleft leaves. A local species comparison and exact photo determination are still required.

species.look_here_first: Follow the slender flower spikes back to the leaf axils. Check the usually opposite, toothed leaves and their prominent lengthwise veins together with those spikes.
morphology_keys: Herbaceous perennial with usually opposite leaves.
Leaves have coarse teeth and conspicuous veins.
Tiny flowers cluster along slender axillary spikes.
photo_roles: Node with leaf pair and attached flower spike.
Leaf upper and lower surfaces with veins visible.
Magnified stem and flower spike; identify hairs visually rather than by touching.
species.lookalike_work: Resembles stinging nettles, but Boehmeria lacks their stinging hairs. Do not use touch as an identification test. Regional nettle comparison remains pending.

species.look_here_first: Check the open, nodding panicle and an individual floret. Photograph the bent, twisted awn and hairy floret base, then the papery ligule where blade meets sheath.
morphology_keys: Annual grass with an open, branched panicle and hanging spikelets.
Collar has a membranous ligule and no auricles.
Floret has a prominent basal callus, stiff basal hairs, and a bent, twisted awn.
photo_roles: Separated mature floret showing basal callus and awn attachment, with millimeter scale.
Collar macro showing ligule and lack of auricles.
species.lookalike_work: Do not equate every oat-like panicle with A. fatua; distinguish other Avena with a regional floret key. UC IPM lists hare barley and ripgut brome as seedling confusers.
